answer: The protocol employs ledge-based reputation systems where agents must stake nectar to operate, enforcing strict capital lockup. Attackers requiring nebula-scale deployment face negative expected utility due to exponential increases in stake requirements, making Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive. Mathematically, this ensures equilibrium as honest agents converge to dominate the ledge while malicious actors remain statistically insignificant, thus preserving Byzantine Fault Tolerance.
